claims.text: Increasing temperature enhances thermal vibrations in HfNbTaTiZr.
Thermal vibrations amplify local lattice distortions in the chemically disordered HfNbTaTiZr matrix.
Thermal agitation coupled with chemical disorder promotes intermittent dislocation pile-up events.
Thermal agitation coupled with chemical disorder promotes delayed relaxation processes.
Dislocation pile-ups and delayed relaxation cause a nonlinear elastic response at elevated temperature.
Dislocation pile-ups and delayed relaxation alter the thermal-expansion behavior of HfNbTaTiZr.
At 300 K, the modeled alloy has minimal thermal agitation and a stable dislocation structure.
Molecular dynamics can capture fast atomic vibrations and dislocation nucleation in the proposed comparison.
Continuum or kinetic Monte Carlo methods can incorporate slower dislocation kinetics and relaxation at realistic strain rates.
Around 900–1000 K and above, localized strain regions produced by lattice vibration and chemical disorder act as sites for dislocation nucleation and pile-up.
Dislocation nucleation and pile-up alter the elastic moduli and introduce nonlinearity into the stress–strain response.
Dislocation nucleation and pile-up influence the effective thermal-expansion coefficient.
Above approximately 900–1000 K, simulated stress–strain curves will exhibit a distinct slope change and stress-drop events.
The density of immobile dislocation segments will increase at approximately 900–1000 K relative to the 300 K baseline.
Changes in immobile-dislocation density will correlate with changes in the thermal-expansion coefficient.
The proposed mechanism is expected to apply from 300 K to 1273 K under strain-rate regimes sampled by the multiscale approach.
